remit: X12 defines this reason as an exact duplicate of a claim or service. X12 limits it to group code OA, except where state workers' compensation rules require CO, so check which group code your payer actually sent.
metaDescription: CO-18 denial explained: the payer sees an exact duplicate claim or service. How to check the original claim, what not to resubmit, and how to prevent it.
summary: The payer says this claim or service duplicates one it already received.
causes: The same claim was submitted twice, for example after a slow acknowledgement
Staff resubmitted instead of checking the status of the first claim
A genuine repeat service was billed without anything to tell it apart
fixes: Look up the first claim; it may already be paid or in process
If it was paid, post the payment and do nothing further
For a genuine repeat service, correct the claim with the appropriate modifier and documentation
prevention: Set a rule for how long to wait before any follow-up on an unacknowledged claim

faqs.question: Should I resubmit a CO-18 claim?
faqs.answer: Not until you have checked the original. Most CO-18 denials mean the first claim is already paid or processing.

faqs.question: How do I avoid CO-18 when a service really was repeated?
faqs.answer: Use the modifier your payer requires for a repeat service and make sure the chart supports a second, separate service.
